content.comment_body: I'm experiencing issues with a [product_name] (cannot confirm exactly, but possibly [article_no]). The entire [product_name] completely locks up, not just the screen or buttons. Screen and outputs remain frozen as they were at the last operational point, and changing inputs or pressing buttons has no effect. Only turning the power off and on will restore it. This is a major issue because it's not possible to set up an internal mechanism to detect such a freeze. The cause for the freeze is unclear, though it has not happened within the first 24 hours after startup. My current workaround is to use a second identical [product_name] in parallel—with the same inputs and program—where both units provide a 1Hz on/off output. You can use a timer relay to power cycle the [product_name] that misses a cycle. However, this solution is costly and not very reliable given the unknown nature of the underlying problem, which ideally shouldn't occur at all. Any suggestions?

To provide accurate advice, it's essential to specify the exact [article_no] and the firmware [version_no] of your [product_name]. There was a case with a [product_name] ([version_no]) where a similar error happened after about 50 days of uninterrupted operation.

analysis.insight_summary: A user describes recurring complete system freezes with their [product_name], affecting all input and output functions and necessitating a manual power restart. The issue is hard to monitor automatically, and the root cause is unknown. The user is concerned about reliability, detectability, and experiences significant operational downtime and frustration due to the freezes.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks reliable and continuous autonomous operation of the [product_name], with internal systems capable of detecting or preventing such freezes so manual intervention and restarts are not required.
